name: PaymentMethodCard
description: One payment method: a generic card mark, the last four digits, the expiry with an expires soon notice, a default badge, and the actions Update, Remove (confirmed) and Make default. With no method it offers Add a payment method. It never holds a full card number; your callbacks do the work. UI permission is not security: the server must check again.

method.tsType: { id: string; brand?: string; last4: string; expMonth: number; expYear: number; holder?: string; isDefault?: boolean }
method.description: The method to show. brand is a short word for the chip (e.g. "Credit"); only the last four digits are ever shown. Leave out for the empty state.

expiresSoonDays.description: How many days before the end of the expiry month the card counts as expiring soon.

now.description: The current date for the expiry check. Defaults to today; pass one for a fixed result in tests and server rendering.

state.description: The data state: loading shows a skeleton, empty (or no method) offers Add a payment method, error shows a message with Try again.

onRetry.description: Adds a Try again button to the error state.

onAdd.description: Starts adding a method from the empty state; yours, async.

onUpdate.tsType: (method: { id: string; brand?: string; last4: string; expMonth: number; expYear: number; holder?: string; isDefault?: boolean }) => void | Promise<unknown>
onUpdate.description: Starts updating the method (usually opens your payment form); yours, async.

onRemove.tsType: (method: { id: string; brand?: string; last4: string; expMonth: number; expYear: number; holder?: string; isDefault?: boolean }) => void | Promise<unknown>
onRemove.description: Removes the method after the person confirmed; yours, async.

onMakeDefault.tsType: (method: { id: string; brand?: string; last4: string; expMonth: number; expYear: number; holder?: string; isDefault?: boolean }) => void | Promise<unknown>
onMakeDefault.description: Makes this the default method; yours, async. The button is not shown on the default method.

permissions.description: What the app allows: add, update, remove and makeDefault. Hidden renders nothing; disabled keeps the control reachable (aria-disabled) with the reason shown and read, and nothing runs. This only changes what people see: the server must check again.

classNames.description: Extra class names for single parts, so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Keys: root, brand, details, number, expiry, badge, notice, actions, updateButton, removeButton, defaultButton, addButton, status.

keyboard: Tab: moves through Update, Make default and Remove
Remove opens a confirmation: Escape cancels
requirements: The card is a group named "Payment method" followed by the last four digits
The brand mark is decorative; the digits are said as text, e.g. "ending in 4242"
Expires soon and Expired are words with an icon, never only a color
Default is a badge with text
Removing needs a confirmation and is announced when done
After a removal focus moves to the card so it is not lost
A disabled action stays focusable and the reason is its description

use_when: Showing the card or method a workspace pays with on a billing page
A list of methods: render one PaymentMethodCard each
avoid_when: Collecting card details: use your payment provider's own fields, never your own inputs
anti_patterns: Treating the permissions prop as protection: UI permission is not security, so the server must check again
Passing a full card number: only the last four digits belong in the browser
Showing a card network logo you do not have the right to: the brand chip is plain text on purpose

contract.data: One payment method (brand word, last four digits, expiry, default flag) and async callbacks to add, update, remove and make default.
